misconception.text: The law of reflection says the angle of reflection equals the angle of incidence, both measured from the surface.

correction.text: Both angles are measured from the normal, the line perpendicular to the surface at the point of incidence. Measuring from the surface gives a different pair of numbers, though the two are complementary.

signal.text: Our own question asks which angle the reflection angle equals.

misconception.text: Snell's law relates the angles of incidence and refraction to the wavelengths in the two media.

correction.text: It relates them to the speeds of light, through the refractive indices. The wavelengths change as the speed changes, and the frequency does not, which is the point of the law.

signal.text: Our own question offers the wavelength reading as an option.

misconception.text: A short-sighted person is given a diverging lens to correct their sight.

correction.text: They are given a converging lens. A short-sighted eye focuses distant light in front of the retina, and a converging lens brings the focus back onto it, which lets the wearer see near objects.

signal.text: Our own question offers the diverging lens as the answer.

misconception.text: The magnifying power of a compound microscope is increased by using an eyepiece of longer focal length.

correction.text: A shorter eyepiece focal length gives a larger angular magnification, because the eyepiece acts as a simple magnifier. A longer objective focal length helps as well.

signal.text: Our own question offers the longer eyepiece as an option.

stem.text: Snell's law relates the angles of incidence and refraction to

options.text: the speeds of light in the two media
the wavelengths in the two media
the intensities in the two media
the polarisations in the two media

explanation.text: Snell's law is $n_1 \sin\theta_1 = n_2 \sin\theta_2$, and the refractive index is the ratio of the speeds, so the law is really about speed.

explanation.text: A short-sighted eye focuses distant light in front of the retina, and a converging lens brings it back onto the retina, so the wearer can see near objects.

stem.text: The magnifying power of a compound microscope is increased by

options.text: using an objective of larger focal length
using an eyepiece of shorter focal length

explanation.text: The eyepiece acts as a simple magnifier, so a shorter focal length gives a larger angular magnification. A longer objective focal length also helps.
